notes.text: Dosa identifies Yonatan as his brother and a student of the House of Shammai, using the epithet bekhor satan.
The Bavli has the epithet and studentship wording. Rashi explains the expression through sharpness and insistence on putting one’s ruling into practice.
Rashi’s sharpness explanation directly matches Heilprin’s first gloss.
The Shammaite dispute names Rabbi Yehoshua among the visitors in the Bavli. The local pointer goes to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chanania.
The Bavli has the direct exchange between Yonatan and Akiva regarding his reputation and his answers.

The Bavli ancestry discussion uses the cognate foolish-firstborn expression for a firstborn to the mother. Heilprin attributes its application here to Rav Tzemach through Yuchasin. That particular attribution still needs a direct witness.
